def: A coding agent that edits its own code, keeps every version in an archive and accepts changes based on benchmark results instead of formal proofs.
Schmidhuber's theoretical self-rewriting system that changes its own code only after proving the change improves its expected reward, which makes it elegant but impractical.
An agent editing its own code (tools, prompts, workflow) to produce a new version of itself, with the underlying model's weights left unchanged.
The random choice of which archived agent to modify next, weighted by a sigmoid of its score times 1/(1 + number of its children).
Testing a candidate on a few tasks first and spending a larger evaluation budget only on those that clear a bar.
Raising the measured score without solving the underlying problem, for example by disabling the logging a detector depends on.
A benchmark that gives an agent a real GitHub repository and issue and checks whether its patch makes hidden tests pass.
The Aider team's benchmark of programming exercises across several languages, used to test coding agents.
The recorded chain of parent-to-child modifications leading to a given agent, which lets reviewers read every change that produced it.
The 1/(1 + children) factor that gives less weight to agents that have already produced many children.
